about: Fine Print's own code signatures, for trackers Exodus does not list. Same rules as Exodus: the signature is a regex searched in slash-separated class names (com/foo/Bar), and '.' matches any character. Ids are fp-<slug>, one entry per tracker ('|' joins several packages). pipeline/fetch_trackers.py merges these into android/app/src/main/assets/trackers.json, which stays under the ODbL like the Exodus data. Every entry must cite evidence a reviewer can re-check; a hit is evidence tier contains_code only.

trackers.name: Arity
evidence: Life360 26.37.0 (versionCode 2924500), base APK SHA-256 e468187c69ffa8439dc0a55705e608ec83387e458d796d5a1ea4ad49bfa8af20 (the same file Exodus report 785809 analysed from Google Play): defines 642 classes under com/arity/coreengine and com/arity/sensor, per the Fine Print APK scan harness on 2026-10-02.

The same APK's manifest registers com.arity.coreengine.driving.CoreEngineForegroundService, com.arity.coreengine.tripinitiator.geofence.service.GeofenceInitiatorService and four com.arity.coreengine receivers; its dex strings include "Driving Logs. Arity SDK is started" and https://api.arity.com/mobileconfigservice/v1/config.

Life360 builds 19.8.0 to 23.27.0 ship the SDK as com.arity.coreEngine.* (capital E), hence both spellings. Signature-verified APKs of MyRadar 8.74.0 and Arity's own Routely 5.4.0 also define CoreEngine classes; across eight APKs (about 344,000 classes) this signature matched every sample and nothing outside com/arity.
The broader com.arity. is avoided on purpose: an unrelated developer (Arity Infoway) publishes apps under com.arity.arityhrmpro and com.arity.newshunt.

Life360 support article 'Arity' (updated 2026-06-01), self-disclosed: "Drive Detection, including Crash Alerts, Driving reports, and Drive history, is powered by Arity." https://support.life360.com/api/v2/help_center/en-us/articles/23053397958551.json
